 L to R: State Sen. Ryan Fazio and Gov. Ned Lamont squared off for the final debate of the gubernatorial campaign before Election Day next week. Credit: Donald Eng / CTNewsJunkie 
 As Election Day dawned in Connecticut, state officials already had received a half-million votes, according to information from Secretary of the State Stephanie Thomas’ office.
 The numbers are unofficial until certified.
 According to Thomas’ office, 455,016 voters had cast a ballot in person during the 14 days of early voting. In addition, the state had received another 58,305 absentee ballots for a total of 513,321 votes cast before Election Day.
 For comparison, in the 2022 election, the most recent statewide election with a governor’s race on the ballot, total turnout was 57.62%, or 1,297,811 votes. So far, that 513,321 early turnout equates to a 22.7% total turnout, or just under 40% of the 2022 total.
 Registered Democrats outvoted their Republican and unaffiliated counterparts in early voting, casting 216,107 votes, or about 47.5% of the total. Democrats represent about 35.6 % of registered voters. Republicans, 21.5% of registered voters, cast 89,115 early votes, about 19.5% of the total. Unaffiliated voters, who represent 41.4% of the electorate, cast 143,739 votes, about 31.5%.
 Of the absentee ballots received before Election Day, 29,881 were returned by registered Democrats, 10,527 by Republicans and 17,104 by unaffiliated voters. In addition, voters registered with minor parties cast 6,859 absentee and in-person early votes.
 West Hartford led the way in early voting, with that town’s voters casting 10,406 early votes. Norwalk (9,822)), Fairfield (9,111), Stamford (8,959) and Milford (8,711) rounded out the top five.
